Description: Flags possible front-running if an employee trade is made the same or next day as a client’s, in the same security, with equal or greater volume.
Flags potential misuse of MNPI if employee's trade volume is >2x the average without any public news.
Flags if an employee trades unusually large volumes on the same day earnings are announced.
Flags traders who place large limit orders and cancel most of them to influence prices (spoofing).
Flags if the same entity is effectively on both sides of the trade (wash trading).
Flags if performance is significantly outpacing the disclosed benchmark due to a hidden mismatch.
Flags if conservative clients are placed in high-risk securities that may violate suitability.

RuleName: Duty of Loyalty: Employee vs. Client
Description: Flags if an employee's personal trade volume overshadows a client's on the same date.
Flags if an employee places trades without explicit client authorization.
Flags if block trades are allocated unfairly among multiple clients.
Flags if a client’s execution price is 50% worse than the current market price (possible best-execution violation).
Flags a scenario where the employee hypes a security, then quickly sells (pump-and-dump).
Flags unusual upward or downward price moves in the final minutes of trading, possibly to manipulate closing prices.
Flags cross trades between two accounts at off-market prices.
Flags if reported performance is inflated more than 20% above actual results.
Flags if an employee prioritizes family accounts ahead of clients.
Flags if employee trades a rumored M&A target before any public announcement.
Flags personal use of soft dollars or excessive commissions for personal gain.
Flags if employee shorts a security just before a bullish research report is published.
Flags if an employee trades a security on the firm's restricted list.
Flags if an employee executes a trade against explicit client instructions.
Flags if trading activity is excessively high in a fee-based account, suggesting churning.
Flags rapid in-and-out trading in mutual funds that could be considered market timing.
Flags if a manager fails to vote proxies in line with client directives.
Flags if margin is used in a client account that is supposed to be cash-only.
Flags if an employee has undisclosed outside business activities.
Flags if referral fees are not properly disclosed to clients.
Flags if similar clients receive different prices for the same security without justification.
Flags contingent commission arrangements that create conflicts of interest.
Flags if employee trades a security just before an internal research upgrade is released.
